newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Little impact on HK-Taipei cargo volumes from EVA.
newsitem.headline: Little impact on HK-Taipei cargo volumes from EVA.

text.p: Two months after EVA Air entered the busy Hong Kong-Taipei sector, the Taiwanese carrier's two main rivals say there has been no significant impact on cargo volumes.

Under a new commercial agreement on air services, EVA began flying 16 times a week between Taipei and Hong Kong on August 1 using Boeing 747 Combi aircraft with 45 tonnes cargo capacity, McDonnell Douglas MD-11s and Boeing 767s. At the launch of the new service, EVA said it expected Hong Kong to quickly become its busiest international destination.
China Airlines and Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd which have flown the route for many years, both said the new competition has so far not had a noticeable impact on load factors.
But China Airlines' Hong Kong cargo manager M. F. Lai told Reuters he is unhappy at EVA's "discounted" rate which is hitting yields.

"I'm not happy about the rate. I don't know why Eva are using such a low rate. We have talked to them face to face and asked them to increase it but their price structure remains the same. It's a difficult situation," Lai said.
China Airlines rate to Taipei was HK$4 per kg until EVA began offering HK$3.50 per kg, Lai said.

"We were only affected by EVA during the first two weeks of their service. We don't see any negative effect since then because the market is ok but wait and see what the real effect is when the market goes down," Lai said.
He called on Eva Air to raise their fares to improve profitability for all carriers on the route.
EVA have so far declined to comment.
Cathay Pacific Cargo's marketing and sales manager Ray Jewell also said EVA has had no significant impact.

"We haven't noticed any significant effect so far but it is the peak right now and things are flowing pretty well when extra capacity would not necessarily have a big impact but come the slack in January and February there may well be more noticeable effects," he said.
The Hong Kong-Taipei route is one of Cathay's busiest with six freighter flights a week and nine passenger flights a day.

China Airlines has five freighter flights a week and 11 passenger flights a day. Lai said his freighter flights are currently enjoying 85 percent load factor. During the slack period load factors are expected to slump to 60 percent.
Other airlines which operate Hong Kong to Taipei services are Thai Airways International Ltd, Malaysia Airlines System Bhd, Singapore Airlines Ltd, Garuda Indonesia and British Airways Plc..

According to new statistics from Hong Kong's Civil Aviation Department, Taipei is Hong Kong's biggest trading partner importing 7,619 tonnes of air cargo and exporting 5,642 tonnes to Taipei during July.

Lai also said he expects the current Hong Kong government estimate of a seven percent increase in the weight of exports from Hong Kong to Taiwan this year to be exceeded which would be good news for his airline. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
